proposed.explanation:
Your premise is the reverse of what the evidence shows. The FY2025 consolidated statement reports net profit of 82,258,815,000 EGP (≈ 82.3 billion) for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, versus 55,256,732,000 EGP (≈ 55.3 billion) for 31 Dec 2024. That is an increase of roughly 49 %, not a one-third decline. The 55-billion figure you saw is the 2024 number, not the 2025 result. Basic EPS moved in the same direction: 18.25 EGP in 2025 vs 14.72 EGP in 2024. Net interest income also grew, from about 91.1 billion to about 107.7 billion EGP. So the headline you read appears to have swapped the two years.

On the question of whether to sell: the evidence points to a company whose earnings are expanding, not contracting. With a five-year horizon and a separate emergency fund, there is no liquidity pressure forcing a sale, and the medium risk tolerance is consistent with holding a large, profitable bank. I would not sell on the basis of a misread headline.

On adding to the position: you already hold 400 shares at 128 EGP = 51,200 EGP, and your cash is 20,000 EGP, giving a total portfolio of 71,200 EGP. COMI already represents about 72 % of that total. The diversification rule caps any single holding at 50 % of total portfolio value after a buy, so you cannot purchase additional COMI shares without breaching that limit. You would need to reduce COMI or add other assets before you could buy more.

Caveats: the evidence provided covers only a few income-statement line items for two years. I do not have balance-sheet data, dividend history, sector outlook, or valuation multiples, so I cannot confirm the stock is fairly priced or that the earnings growth will persist. The recommendation to hold is based on correcting the factual error in your question and the absence of any negative signal in the available data; it is not a guarantee of future performance. Bank earnings remain sensitive to interest-rate policy, credit quality, and macroeconomic conditions in Egypt, all of which carry uncertainty over a five-year horizon.

The recommendation is based solely on the provided evidence and does not constitute a guarantee of future returns.
